newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: BCCI creditors in UAE start getting repaid - paper.
newsitem.headline: BCCI creditors in UAE start getting repaid - paper.

text.p: Local banks have recently started reimbursing creditors of United Arab Emirates branches of the failed Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI), local newspapers reported on Monday.

They said banks had started issuing cheques to depositors with claims exceeding 20,000 dirhams ($5,450). The global liquidators are responsible for paying these depositors 24.5 percent of their claims.
The papers also said small depositors were getting repaid.
The UAE Liquidation Administration has said that the UAE Central Bank will make payment in full to depositors with claims of up to 20,000 dirhams, a move independent of the global liquidators.
In the UAE, there are about 45,000 creditors, owed nearly five billion dirhams ($1.4 billion).
BCCI, founded in Luxembourg in 1972, was shut down in 1991 with debts of over $12 billion after evidence emerged of widespread money laundering.
